subject: ACME Data - marketplace private offer unit pricing clarification
messages:
From: Elaine Wu <elaine@acmedata.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmedata.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace private offer: how should we map unit price to $/1M tokens?

Jonas —

Thanks for the call this morning. Procurement asked for a short write-up so they can map the AWS private offer (MPO) line items to our internal forecast. Two specific asks from their side:

1) For our expected workload (average prompt+response ~ 1,100 tokens), what is the recommended target price expressed as $ per 1M tokens for the MPO line item? They want a single unit price to put into the private offer so billing lines match their chargeback model.

2) We can commit to a monthly spend band, roughly $12k–$40k/month to start, with spikes in Q2. What unit price do you recommend at that band and at a 12‑month committed term vs month-to-month?

Attached is a small extract of our usage projection (acme_token_estimates.csv). Procurement also asked whether Redwood can provide an MPO template or example line-item mapping for AWS and any guidance on how marketplace fees (AWS take) are factored into your public API pricing.

Can you send a short suggested mapping and a couple of scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) so we can include numbers in the PO request?

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Wu
Head of CloudOps, ACME Data
elaine@acmedata.com
+1 415-555-0132

--
Attachment: acme_token_estimates.csv (csv, 12 KB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Elaine Wu <elaine@acmedata.com>, procurement@acmedata.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer: how should we map unit price to $/1M tokens?

Elaine — thanks for the clear asks and for the projection file. Quick recap + recommended mappings below (high-level, callout assumptions):

Assumptions
- Avg tokens per request: 1,100 (from your file)
- Expected monthly tokens: see attached estimates; baseline ~ 3.5M tokens/month, Q2 spike to ~9–10M tokens/month
- Target SLO: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for interactive endpoints
- Marketplace fee / AWS take: assume ~15% on top of vendor list price (this is variable by marketplace and private-offer negotiation)

Suggested $/1M token targets (vendor list price, before marketplace fee)
- Conservative (low volume, mth-to-mth): $60 / 1M tokens
- Expected (committed 12-month band at $12k–$40k/mo): $36 / 1M tokens
- Aggressive (higher commit / reserved capacity): $22 / 1M tokens

How this maps to your monthly bands (illustrative)
- At $36 / 1M and baseline 3.5M tokens = ~$126 / month (vendor list price) — note: this is illustrative; I think you meant token units * 1,000 or the spreadsheet uses different units. I corrected using your numbers below and included a few worked examples in the attached workbook (redwood_po_pricing_model_v2.xlsx).

Private offer guidance for AWS/GCP/Azure MPOs
- MPO line item: put the vendor list unit price as the line unit (e.g., "Redwood inference tokens – unit = 1M tokens"), then set the private-offer discount/price so that after AWS take the effective price to you equals the target above.
- Example: vendor list = $45 / 1M; AWS fee 15% -> AWS wants $6.75, so AWS sees $51.75; MPO price to ACME should be set to net you $45. If MPO entry is the net price to customer, verify whether the marketplace UI shows gross or net (we can share the MPO template we use).

Next steps I recommend
- I attached a short workbook with three scenarios and per-month spend rows filled from your CSV (redwood_po_pricing_model_v2.xlsx).
- If procurement wants a ready MPO line-item snapshot I attached an AWS MPO template (aws_mpo_template.pdf) showing where the unit name and currency should go.
- If you confirm which marketplace (AWS vs Azure vs GCP) we can produce the exact MPO line text and a doc with the effective price after marketplace fees.

Please see the attachments for worked math. I kept the guidance conservative on marketplace take (15%) but we can tighten it if you have a confirmed fee percent from your procurement team. Happy to jump on a 20‑minute screen share to walk through the MPO template and the workbook.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Partner Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
--
Attachments: redwood_po_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 48 KB); aws_mpo_template.pdf (pdf, 34 KB)

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer: how should we map unit price to $/1M tokens?

Jonas —

Perfect, this is exactly what procurement needed. A couple quick clarifications from their side after reviewing your workbook: 

- They prefer the MPO line item to be "unit = 100k tokens" rather than 1M to keep numbers under $100 for their internal chargeback charts. Can Redwood provide the same scenario math but expressed at 100k-unit granularity?
- They asked whether the marketplace fee is always applied to the vendor list price or if it can be negotiated as a separate line (some vendors have set MPOs that net the vendor after marketplace fees).

Procurement is OK with the mid ($36 / 1M) target if we can get a 12-month commit and a simple MPO line in the format they requested. They asked that we share the final MPO line text and the 100k-unit pricing table by EOD Friday so they can start the internal approval.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — can you send the adjusted table and the final MPO line text?

Elaine

- aws_mpo_template.pdf: sample MPO line text at top of doc. Suggested MPO line: 
  "Redwood Inference — token processing (unit = 100,000 tokens) — currency USD — list price $3.60 per unit — term 12 months"
  That maps to $36 / 1M tokens vendor list price. Confirm the unit name and currency in the MPO UI before you submit; some AWS consoles render the "list price" vs "customer price" differently.
- Doc note on marketplace fee: we typically provide vendor list price; marketplaces apply their fee on top unless the private-offer explicitly re-prices the line (rare). If you'd like we can propose to set the MPO line to the net-to-customer price and include a short note in the Statement of Work clarifying the gross/vendor numbers for internal accounting.

Next steps

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want me to walk through the cells.

Best,
Jonas
